label: TP
reason: User input from request parameters flows directly into the cookie value via param -> str assignment. Although ESAPI encoder is applied to str before HTML output, the primary alert (java/xss) targets the concatenation point where unencoded user data is written to the response stream. The encoder protects the logged message content but does not sanitize the cookie value itself, allowing XSS via the HTTP response header. The http-response-splitting alert confirms user-controlled content reaches the response layer.

evidence.note: User param flows to str, then to cookie value and response output; encoder only protects log message, not cookie
